newsitem.title: MALI: Mali president announces legislative poll delay.
newsitem.headline: Mali president announces legislative poll delay.

text.p: President Alpha Oumar Konare has said that legislative polls launching Mali's second multi-party elections will be put back from March 9 at the request of the independent national electoral commission.

Konare told a meeting on security on Thursday that a new date for the elections would be announced next week by the government after the necessary consultations with the commission, which had asked for more time to organise.
But he confirmed that presidential elections would take place as planned on May 4 and 18.
"All the elections will take place before June 8 1997 in conformity with the constitution," he said, in response to opposition suggestions that the election timetable would be totally changed.
Municipal elections are due to be held on June 1.
Konare, a historian, won a five-year term as president in Mali's widely praised 1992 democratic transition and is seeking a second term.
His supporters, grouped in the Alliance for Democracy in Mali or ADEMA, had a majority in the old 116-seat national assembly. The new assembly will have 147 seats.
The opposition is grouped in two main alliances, the Rally of Patriotic Forces (RFP), and the newly formed Front for Change and Democracy (FCD).
Mali's last elections followed the 1991 overthrow of dictator Moussa Traore by soldiers, led by General Amadou Toumani Toure, who ushered in civilian rule and stepped down.
